ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in rectangle $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. Lines parallel to $AC$ and $BD$ are drawn through points $D$ and $C$ respectively, intersecting at point $E$. Quadrilateral $OCED$ is a rhombus. If $AB=3$ and $BC=4$, what is the area of the rhombus $OCED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $AB=3$, $BC=4$,\\
thus, the area of rectangle $ABCD$ equals $3\times 4=12$,\\
since $S_{\triangle ODC}=\frac{1}{4}S_{\text{rectangle}ABCD}=3$,\\
therefore, the area of the quadrilateral $OCED$ equals $2S_{\triangle ODC}=\boxed{6}$.
